newsitem.title: CANADA: Kinross files to buy back shrs, debentures.
newsitem.headline: Kinross files to buy back shrs, debentures.

text.p: Kinross Gold Corp said on Wednesday it filed with the Toronto Stock Exchange to buy back up to five percent of its common stock and up to C$10 million of its 5.5 percent convertible debentures.

The Toronto-based mining company said that over the next 12 months it may buy up to 6.24 million of its 124.8 million currently issued and outstanding shares. The C$10 million in debentures Kinross filed to buy back represents five percent of its C$200 million of debentures outstanding.

Kinross also said that its second-quarter cash operating costs declined to about US$256 per ounce of gold from the US$307 an ounce reported in the first quarter. Gold equivalent production in the second quarter was about 124,000 ounces, up 12 percent from the first quarter.

The second-quarter costs include cash operating costs from the Macassa mine of about US$417 an ounce due to a series of rockbursts, Kinross said. The company said costs at its largest mine, Hoyle Pond, declined in the second quarter to US$177 per ounce, with further reductions projected for the rest of the year.

"Clearly, in the current gold price environment, the company is actively and critically reviewing all aspects of its operations. It is our intention to ensure that for the balance of the year, the company can both maintain its growth profile at Hoyle Pond and remain, at current metal prices, cash neutral from operations," the company said in a statement. Hoyle Pond is in northern Ontario.
Kinross noted it had about US$190 million available for acquisitions and said it was well positioned to review growth opportunities.
Shares of Kinross rose 0.15 to 5.10 in Toronto Stock Exchange trading of more than 1.37 million shares today.
